action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find
tools.description: Search the current page in the Browser pane for elements whose accessibility-tree line (role / name / text) contains `query`, case-insensitively. Returns up to 20 `ref_N` matches usable with `computer`/`form_input`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

query.description: Text to look for in an element's role, name or text (case-insensitive substring, e.g. "Sign in", "search", "Add to cart").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__form_input
tools.description: Set the value of a form element identified by `ref` (from read_page/find). Handles input/textarea/select/checkbox/contenteditable.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

ref.description: Element reference ID from the read_page tool (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2")

value.description: The value to set. For checkboxes use boolean, for selects use option value or text, for other inputs use appropriate string/number

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this form fill does on the page and to what, for example 'Sets the delivery date to 29 September'. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract the visible text of the Browser pane's page (article/main content first, falls back to body innerText).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__javascript_tool
tools.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes — edit source code instead.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description: Action to perform (only `javascript_exec` is supported).

text.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Evaluated in the page context with REPL semantics: top-level `await` works, and the result of the last expression is returned automatically — write the expression you want (e.g. `window.myData.value`, or `await fetch(url).then(r=>r.json())`) rather than `return ...`. Return values are serialized as JSON.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__navigate
tools.description: Navigate the Browser pane to a URL, or go "back"/"forward" in history. If the Browser pane isn't open yet, this opens it at the URL (no dev server needed).

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

force.description: If the page shows a "Leave site?" dialog because of unsaved changes, discard those changes and navigate anyway. Defaults to false.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
tools.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
tools.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start

name.description: Server name from .claude/launch.json.

url.description: URL to open in the Browser pane without a dev server (instead of starting one by `name`).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
tools.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_console_messages
tools.description: Get console output (log, info, warn, error, debug) from the Browser pane.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

limit.description: Max entries to return (default: 50, max: 200).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_network_requests
tools.description: List network requests, or fetch a specific response body by `requestId`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

urlPattern.description: Substring filter on the request URL as listed (auth values show as REDACTED).

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this request instead of listing.

limit.description: Max entries to return when listing (default: 50).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__read_page
tools.description: Read the current page in the Browser pane as a YAML-style accessibility tree. Each interactive element is tagged `[ref_N]` for use with `computer`/`form_input`/`find`. Prefer this over screenshot for verifying text and structure. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default; if it exceeds the limit it is truncated with a note — pass a larger max_chars, or use ref_id/depth to focus.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

filter.description: 'interactive' returns only clickable/typable elements; 'all' (default) returns the full tree.

ref_id.description: Restrict the tree to descendants of this `ref_N` (from a previous read_page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_close
tools.description: Close one Browser pane tab. Closing the last tab closes the Browser pane itself (reopen it with `preview_start`).

tabId.description: Tab to close.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_context
tools.description: List every Browser pane tab (origin only — titles are page-authored). Returns {browserOpen, tabs: [{tabId, origin, isActive}]} plus a line saying whether the pane is currently displayed or hidden (a hidden pane still works, but its page runs as a background page, so timing and performance numbers from it can be off; prefer `read_page` / `get_page_text` over screenshots while it is hidden). browserOpen is false (and tabs empty) until `preview_start` or `navigate` opens the pane, so you don't need to call this before opening it.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_create
tools.description: Open a fresh blank Browser pane tab; returns the new tabId. Opens in the background by default — set `foreground: true` when the user wants to watch. Prefer `preview_start` with a `url` when you know the destination; use `navigate` to load a URL into a blank tab.

foreground.description: Front the new tab (user asked to see it or is following along). Default false: open behind the user's current tab.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__tabs_select
tools.description: Front the given Browser pane tab. Background tabs keep running while you drive them, so front one only when the user should look — or for a page that pauses itself while hidden (e.g. a video player).

tabId.description: Tab to front.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

tools.name: mcp__computer-use__app_ax_find
tools.description:
Search the accessibility elements captured by the last app_screenshot of one window. Filter by role (e.g. "AXTextArea", "AXButton") and/or title substring. Returns matching elements with their [N] index — pass that as element_index to app_click/app_type. tools.name: mcp__computer-use__app_key

GitHub's documentation indicates that when a repository has more than one copy of a community health file, the **.github folder wins, then the repository root, then the docs folder**. This applies to CONTRIBUTING files. If a repository contains more than one CONTRIBUTING file, the file shown in links is chosen from the .github directory, then the root directory, and finally the docs directory. The same order applies to READMEs, per the GitHub README documentation, and the default-file docs state that GitHub uses this same precedence for supported files that can be stored in more than one location.

For SECURITY.md, the docs say you can place the file in the repository's root, docs, or .github folder. The results I found don't spell out a separate precedence list for SECURITY.md, so the general order above is the best-supported answer, though it's worth confirming against the current docs.

Two related points:
- **Fallback to the default:** If a repository has no file of that type, GitHub can show one from the owner's `.github` repository instead. If no corresponding file is found in the current repository, GitHub will use the default file from the .github repository.
- **Default-file storage:** FUNDING.yml, VULNERABILITY_REPORT.yml, and VULNERABILITY_REPORT.yaml belong in the .github folder of the default-files repo. The other supported files can go in the root, .github, or docs folder.

Sources: GitHub Docs pages on default community health files, setting contributor guidelines, adding a security policy, and README files.

If a repository contains more than one CONTRIBUTING file, the file shown in links is chosen from the .github directory, then the root directory, and finally the docs directory. The same order applies to READMEs, per the GitHub README documentation, and the default-file docs state that GitHub uses this same precedence for supported files that can be stored in more than one location.

For SECURITY.md, the docs say you can place the file in the repository's root, docs, or .github folder. The results I found don't spell out a separate precedence list for SECURITY.md, so the general order above is the best-supported answer, though it's worth confirming against the current docs.

Two related points:
- **Fallback to the default:** If a repository has no file of that type, GitHub can show one from the owner's `.github` repository instead. If no corresponding file is found in the current repository, GitHub will use the default file from the .github repository.
- **Default-file storage:** FUNDING.yml, VULNERABILITY_REPORT.yml, and VULNERABILITY_REPORT.yaml belong in the .github folder of the default-files repo. The other supported files can go in the root, .github, or docs folder.

Sources: GitHub Docs pages on default community health files, setting contributor guidelines, adding a security policy, and README files.

content.text:
Every file a visitor sees on v2's `main` is a byte-for-byte copy of OrcaSlicer's, and so is the repo's About box. v1 had only ever changed its README, so the README is the one file worth borrowing from. About half of it carries over, but its pitch contradicts what v2 has decided. I haven't changed anything.

**What a visitor sees today, and what should happen to it** (these are my proposals):
- **Front-page README:** this is OrcaSlicer's. It sends people to orcaslicer.com and OrcaSlicer's Discord and wiki. I'd replace it with a new fork-owned `.github/README.md`, which GitHub shows ahead of the root file.
- **`SECURITY.md`:** it tells people to email security bugs to OrcaSlicer's maintainer. This one matters most. GitHub picks `.github/` ahead of the root for these files too, so a fork-owned `.github/SECURITY.md` fixes it without touching upstream's file.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md`:** this is OrcaSlicer's review process. Same fix: a short `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- **Sponsor button (`.github/FUNDING.yml`):** it sends money to SoftFever. I'd delete it. v1 had this too.
- **Issue forms:** they say "Orca Slicer", give OrcaSlicer's log folders, and link to OrcaSlicer's tracker, Discord and Discussions. These files can't be overridden, only edited or replaced. That costs a conflict whenever upstream changes them, as 2.5.0 did.
- **Not verified:** the issue settings turn blank issues off. JusPrin's printer chat opens `JusPrin/issues/new?title=…&body=…` with no template. My hypothesis is that a visitor who isn't a maintainer lands on the template chooser and loses the pre-filled report. Testing it needs a GitHub account with no write access.
- **About box:** the description is OrcaSlicer's ("G-code generator for 3D printers…"), and the website link is OrcaSlicer's Discord invite. These are repo settings, not files.
- **Releases:** "Latest" is v1.4.0, and a 2025 "JusPrin Nightly Builds" pre-release is still listed. Any "Download" link hands people v1 until a v2 release is published.
- **Wiki tab:** it's switched on but empty. I'd switch it off.

**What carries over from v1's README:**
- **Verbatim:** the logo header, the AGPL license lineage (OrcaSlicer, Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer, Slic3r), and the thank-you to OrcaSlicer, with its link updated to `OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer`.
- **The shape:** Why, Download, Getting Started, Feedback, License.
- **Doesn't carry over:**
  - "First GenAI app" and "no manual slicing… Just print". v2's first screen says "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints."
  - "JusBot". v2 calls the feature "AI".
  - "Linux coming soon". v2's release workflow already builds Linux.
  - The getting-started steps. v2 starts with a choice: sign in, your own API key, Claude Code or Claude Desktop, or just slice.
  - A table of contents entry for a "Known Issues" section that doesn't exist.

**Decision needed: the README's pitch.** v1 promised "no manual slicing". v2's first screen leads with "The AI slicer that fixes failed prints", plus a subtitle about showing it a photo and the AI changing the settings and slicing again. Using v2's lines keeps the front page and the app saying the same thing, at the cost of dropping v1's broader promise. Writing a new pitch costs a round of wording. My pick is v2's lines. Should the README lead with them?

**Decision needed: where visitors reach you.** v1 sent feedback to k@obico.io, and nothing in v2 names a community channel. The security policy, the issue forms' "ask a question" link and the About box all need an address. Options:
- k@obico.io everywhere. Simplest, but it puts your inbox on a public page.
- A separate security address plus GitHub Issues for everything else.
- A JusPrin Discord, if one exists.

My pick is the second. Which addresses should these pages use?

Sources: [GitHub Docs: default community health files](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file), [About READMEs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-readmes), [Configuring issue templates](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository)

JusPrin

**Welcome to JusPrin, the first GenAI app for 3D printing!** Brought to you by the creator of [The Spaghetti Detective](https://www.thespaghettidetective.com/), JusPrin aims to revolutionize the 3D printing experience by eliminating the need for manual slicing. Imagine: **no confusing slicing parameters, no headaches over printing issues caused by incorrect settings. Just print.** That's the promise of JusPrin. ## Table of Contents - [Why JusPrin?](#why-jusprin) - [Download](#download) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [Feedback](#feedback) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) ## Why JusPrin? 3D printing enthusiasts have relied on slicing tools to prepare models, often struggling with complex parameters and trial-and-error setups. JusPrin changes that by putting AI in charge of the slicing settings. # Security Policy

If you find a security problem in JusPrin, please report it privately so it can be fixed before it is public.

## Reporting a security problem

- Email [jusprin-support@obico.io](mailto:jusprin-support@obico.io) with **SECURITY** in the subject line.
- Please don't open a public issue or pull request for it.
- Say which JusPrin version and operating system you used. In the app, the version is in **Help › About JusPrin**.
- Describe what an attacker could do, who could be affected, and the steps to reproduce it.

We'll reply to your email, may ask for more detail, and will tell you when a fix is released.

## Problems in OrcaSlicer or other components

JusPrin is built on [OrcaSlicer](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer). If the problem is also in OrcaSlicer, you're welcome to report it to us; we'll pass it on to OrcaSlicer's maintainers. Report problems in third-party libraries to their maintainers.

input.content:
# Contributing to JusPrin

Thanks for wanting to help!

## Reporting a problem

- In the app, use **Help › Report a problem…**. It opens a GitHub issue with your app version and system filled in.
- Or open an issue with the bug report form. Attach the project file and the log folder; the form says where to find them.
- Search the existing issues first. If yours is there, add a comment instead.
- For a security problem, don't open an issue. Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
- For questions, write to [jusprin-support@obico.io](mailto:jusprin-support@obico.io).

JusPrin is built on [OrcaSlicer](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer). If a slicing problem also happens in OrcaSlicer, report it to OrcaSlicer as well, since a fix there reaches JusPrin with the next OrcaSlicer release JusPrin takes.

## Pull requests

- Open an issue first for anything larger than a small fix, so we can agree on the approach.
- Keep each pull request to one topic.
- Explain why the change is needed and how you tested it. Add an automated test when the code can be tested.
- JusPrin's own code lives in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Changes to OrcaSlicer's files must be small, because each one has to be carried forward whenever JusPrin takes a new OrcaSlicer release.
- AI tools are welcome. You are still responsible for the change, so test it and make sure you understand it.

## Building

Follow OrcaSlicer's [How to build](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/how_to_build) guide. JusPrin also needs Node.js and npm to build its AI and Home pages.

## License

By contributing, you agree that your contribution is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3, like the rest of JusPrin.

- For a security problem, don't open an issue. Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

JusPrin is built on [OrcaSlicer](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer). If a slicing problem also happens in OrcaSlicer, report it to OrcaSlicer as well, since a fix there reaches JusPrin with the next OrcaSlicer release JusPrin takes.

## Pull requests

- Open an issue first for anything larger than a small fix, so we can agree on the approach.
- Keep each pull request to one topic.
- Explain why the change is needed and how you tested it. Add an automated test when the code can be tested.
- JusPrin's own code lives in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. Changes to OrcaSlicer's files must be small, because each one has to be carried forward whenever JusPrin takes a new OrcaSlicer release.
- AI tools are welcome. You are still responsible for the change, so test it and make sure you understand it.

## Building

Follow OrcaSlicer's [How to build](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/how_to_build) guide. JusPrin also needs Node.js and npm to build its AI and Home pages.

input.content:
name: 🐞 Bug report
description: JusPrin does something wrong, crashes or freezes
labels: ["bug"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        **Thank you for reporting a problem with JusPrin.**

        The quickest way to report one is **Help › Report a problem…** in the app, which fills in your app version and system.

        Please search the existing issues first. If yours is there, add a comment instead. For a security problem, email jusprin-support@obico.io instead of opening an issue.
  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes:
      label: JusPrin version
      description: The version is in the app's About JusPrin window.
      placeholder: e.g. 2.0.0
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: dropdown
    id: os_type
    attributes:
      label: Operating system
      multiple: true
      options:
        - Windows
        - macOS
        - Linux
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: os_version
    attributes:
      label: Operating system version
      placeholder: e.g. Windows 11, macOS 15.3, Ubuntu 24.04
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: printer
    attributes:
      label: Printer
      placeholder: e.g. Bambu Lab P1S, Prusa MK4, Voron 2.4
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: what_happened
    attributes:
      label: What happened
      description: Include a screenshot if you can. If you were talking to AI, say what you asked and what it did.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: expected
    attributes:
      label: What you expected
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: steps
    attributes:
      label: Steps to make it happen again
      placeholder: |
        1. Open '...'
        2. Click '...'
        3. See the problem
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: files
    attributes:
      label: Project file and log folder
      description: |
        Attach the files with the **Paste, drop, or click to add files** control under this box. Zip anything that is not a `.log`, `.txt` or image, since GitHub rejects other file types, and keep each file under 25 MB.

        * The **project file**, zipped: **File › Export › Project 3MF…**
        * The **log folder**, zipped. **Help › Show Configuration Folder** opens the folder that holds it, or find it at:
          * Windows: `%APPDATA%\JusPrin2\log`
          * macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/log`
          * Linux: `~/.config/JusPrin2/log`
        * If the zip is over 25 MB, attach only the newest log files.
    validations:
      required: false

The search didn't turn up an official GitHub statement on whether `mailto:` is allowed in `contact_links`, but several real-world configs use it.

- **Official GitHub docs:** The docs describe `contact_links` as the way to send people to external sites, and their example uses only `https` URLs. Contact links let you direct people to external sites when you prefer to receive certain reports outside of GitHub.
- **Mailto in the wild:** Outline's GitHub config has a contact link whose URL is a `mailto:` address for hosted support. Mbed TLS uses a `mailto:` address for its security team, with a note that it's for reporting vulnerabilities. Both appear to be working GitHub repo configs, which suggests GitHub accepts the scheme.
- **Fedora/Forgejo docs:** These show `mailto:` links in `contact_links`, but they document Forgejo, not GitHub, so they don't settle the GitHub question.

Bottom line: `mailto:` appears to work in practice, but I couldn't confirm it in GitHub's own documentation. Testing it in a real repo's issue chooser would settle it.

content.text: Shown in the next-step box. Your closing message is your answer to the user: write it now, in full, as the last thing you say this turn. The box asks your question, so do not ask it again.

I've drafted JusPrin's own versions of the files a GitHub visitor sees, and OrcaSlicer's issue forms and sponsor button are removed. Everything is staged in the `ui-walkthrough` checkout but not committed or pushed. The README opens with v1's "first GenAI app… Just print." line as you asked, and every contact point uses jusprin-support@obico.io. The rendered README is attached above.

**The files.** Except for `config.yml`, every file I added is new, so none of them will conflict when the fork takes a future OrcaSlicer release:
- **[.github/README.md](.github/README.md):** v1's README, updated for v2.
  - **Kept from v1:** the opening line and paragraph, the "Why JusPrin?" intro, the Download link, the whole license section, and the thank-you to OrcaSlicer, with its link now pointing at `OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer`.
  - **Rewritten for v2:**
    - The logo is now the soft-serve mark.
    - "JusBot" is now "AI".
    - "Linux coming soon" became "Windows, macOS and Linux".
    - The getting-started steps now cover the v2 choices: a JusPrin account, your own API key, Claude Code or Claude Desktop, or just slice.
    - Feedback now points to **Help › Report a problem…** and the support address.
    - There's a new line saying v1 lives on the `jusprin-v1` branch.
  - GitHub shows this file on the front page ahead of OrcaSlicer's root `README.md`, which stays untouched.
- **[.github/SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md):** asks people to email jusprin-support@obico.io with SECURITY in the subject line. It promises no response times; OrcaSlicer's promised a reply within 7 days.
- **[.github/CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md):** how to report a problem, short pull-request rules, and building via OrcaSlicer's guide plus Node.js.
- **Issue forms:**
  - A JusPrin bug form, covering crashes too. It points to the app's `JusPrin2` log folder, which I confirmed on this Mac, and to **File › Export › Project 3MF…**.
  - A short ideas form.
  - OrcaSlicer's three forms are deleted. When upstream edits one of them, git will stop on that file, and the right answer is always to keep it deleted.
- **`config.yml`:** I edited this OrcaSlicer file in place. It now turns blank issues on, so the app's pre-filled "Report a problem" link opens a form for anyone. It also lists one contact link, to the support email.
- **`FUNDING.yml`:** deleted, which removes the Sponsor button that paid SoftFever.

**Not verified:**
- GitHub checks issue forms only once they're on the default branch. Two things should be looked at after the push: that both forms appear in the chooser, and that the `mailto:` contact link is accepted. Other public repos use `mailto:` there, but GitHub's docs only show `https` links.
- "Linux" in the README is my inference from the release workflow, which builds a Linux version. No v2 release exists yet.

**Still to do. These are repo settings, so I haven't touched them:**
- The About box still shows OrcaSlicer's description, and its website link is OrcaSlicer's Discord.
- The empty Wiki tab is still switched on.
- "Latest release" is still v1.4.0, so the README's Download link gives people v1 until v2 ships.
- The old "JusPrin Nightly Builds" pre-release from 2025 is still listed.

Sources: [GitHub Docs: configuring issue templates](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository), [Outline's config.yml](https://igit.yuuza.net/yuuza/outline/commit/f8077e212542fa4b125b4a5359cf4350bb5e685c), [Mbed TLS config.yml](https://pigweed.googlesource.com/third_party/github/ARMmbed/mbedtls/+/a73b57774451017a0499e24b22c99ae850093471/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml)

Exit code 1
# JusPrin's publisher and version, for everything the build stamps with them:
# the Windows version resource (src/dev-utils/platform/msw/OrcaSlicer.rc.in)
# and the package (packaging.cmake). The top-level CMakeLists.txt includes
# this file right after version.inc, before any of them is configured.
#
# The product name is SLIC3R_APP_NAME, which version.inc already sets to
# JusPrin.

set(JUSPRIN_VENDOR "Obico")

# JusPrin's version lives in one place, Version.hpp; the release workflow
# reads it from there too.
set(_jusprin_version_header "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp")
file(STRINGS "${_jusprin_version_header}" _jusprin_version_line REGEX "kVersion\\[\\] = \"")
if (NOT _jusprin_version_line MATCHES "\"(([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)\\.([0-9]+)[^\"]*)\"")
    message(FATAL_ERROR "No kVersion = \"X.Y.Z\" line in ${_jusprin_version_header}")
endif ()
set(JUSPRIN_VERSION "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
set(JUSPRIN_VERSION_MAJOR "${CMAKE_MATCH_2}")
set(JUSPRIN_VERSION_MINOR "${CMAKE_MATCH_3}")
set(JUSPRIN_VERSION_PATCH "${CMAKE_MATCH_4}")
# Re-run CMake when the version changes, so the resource and package follow it.
set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "${_jusprin_version_header}")

# JusPrin's package identity. The top-level CMakeLists.txt includes this file
# just before include(CPack), so each value set here replaces OrcaSlicer's.
#
# Without it the Windows installer calls itself OrcaSlicer by SoftFever,
# version 2.4.2, and uses OrcaSlicer's uninstall key. Because OrcaSlicer turns
# on CPACK_NSIS_ENABLE_UNINSTALL_BEFORE_INSTALL, that installer would first
# uninstall a real OrcaSlicer. With the key "JusPrin", the one JusPrin 1.x
# used, installing 2.x replaces 1.x instead.
#
# The macOS app and the Linux AppImage get the same identity in the release
# workflow (.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml), which renames and edits
# them after the build.
#
# The version and publisher come from identity.cmake, which the Windows
# version resource of orca-slicer.exe reads too.

set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MAJOR "${JUSPRIN_VERSION_MAJOR}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_MINOR "${JUSPRIN_VERSION_MINOR}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION_PATCH "${JUSPRIN_VERSION_PATCH}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VERSION "${JUSPRIN_VERSION}")

set(CPACK_PACKAGE_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_VENDOR "${JUSPRIN_VENDOR}")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_DESCRIPTION_SUMMARY "JusPrin, the AI-piloted 3D printing slicer built on OrcaSlicer")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_HOMEPAGE_URL "https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_INSTALL_DIRECTORY "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_INSTALL_REGISTRY_KEY "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_DISPLAY_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_PACKAGE_NAME "JusPrin")
set(CPACK_NSIS_URL_INFO_ABOUT "${CPACK_PACKAGE_HOMEPAGE_URL}")
# NSIS needs a backslash before the file name, as in OrcaSlicer's value.
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/images\\\\JusPrin.ico")
set(CPACK_NSIS_MUI_ICON "${CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON}")
set(CPACK_NSIS_MUI_UNIICON "${CPACK_PACKAGE_ICON}")
# The executable keeps OrcaSlicer's file name; the shortcuts are called JusPrin.
set(CPACK_PACKAGE_EXECUTABLES "orca-slicer;JusPrin")
# Not used (the generator is NSIS), but never OrcaSlicer's upgrade code.
set(CPACK_WIX_UPGRADE_GUID "4f6d1c0e-6a3b-4b0e-9a57-3d2c8e1f7b42")

# Keep OrcaSlicer's architecture suffix (_x64, _arm64) and swap the rest.
set(_jusprin_orca_file_prefix "OrcaSlicer_Windows_Installer_V${SoftFever_VERSION}")
string(FIND "${CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME}" "${_jusprin_orca_file_prefix}" _jusprin_prefix_at)
if (NOT _jusprin_prefix_at EQUAL 0)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "OrcaSlicer's installer name changed to '${CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME}'; "
                        "update src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/packaging.cmake to match.")
endif ()
string(REPLACE "${_jusprin_orca_file_prefix}" "JusPrin_Windows_Installer_V${JUSPRIN_VERSION}"
       CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME "${CPACK_PACKAGE_FILE_NAME}")

# On Windows, OrcaSlicer makes itself the handler of orcaslicer:// links each
# time it starts and when its Preferences dialog closes (GUI_App.cpp), without
# asking. JusPrin leaves those links to OrcaSlicer; the links it opens are the
# ones a person chooses in its Preferences (JusPrin/Preferences).
if (SLIC3R_GUI)
    target_compile_definitions(libslic3r_gui PRIVATE SLIC3R_NO_ORCASLICER_URL_ASSOCIATION)
endif ()

# CMake writes every macOS app bundle's Info.plist from OrcaSlicer's
# cmake/modules/MacOSXBundleInfo.plist.in. JusPrin's bundles use a copy that
# has JusPrin's bundle identifier and no CFBundleURLTypes. That template asks
# macOS to send orcaslicer:// links, such as Thingiverse's and MakerWorld's
# "Open in Orca Slicer" buttons, to the app; JusPrin must leave them to
# OrcaSlicer. JusPrin answers no link on macOS: its "Open in slicer" links
# (Printables, Thingiverse) are a Windows feature, see JusPrin/Preferences.
if (APPLE)
    set(_jusprin_plist "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/jusprin/MacOSXBundleInfo.plist.in")
    configure_file("${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/modules/MacOSXBundleInfo.plist.in" "${_jusprin_plist}.orca" COPYONLY)
    configure_file("${_jusprin_plist}.orca" "${_jusprin_plist}.edit" COPYONLY)
    foreach (_jusprin_plist_edit "-remove;CFBundleURLTypes" "-replace;CFBundleIdentifier;-string;io.jusprin.JusPrin")
        execute_process(COMMAND plutil ${_jusprin_plist_edit} "${_jusprin_plist}.edit"
                        RESULT_VARIABLE _jusprin_plist_result ERROR_VARIABLE _jusprin_plist_error)
        if (NOT _jusprin_plist_result EQUAL 0)
            string(REPLACE ";" " " _jusprin_plist_edit "${_jusprin_plist_edit}")
            message(FATAL_ERROR "OrcaSlicer's MacOSXBundleInfo.plist.in changed (plutil ${_jusprin_plist_edit}: "
                                "${_jusprin_plist_error}); update src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/packaging.cmake to match.")
        endif ()
    endforeach ()
    # Rewrite the template only when it changes, so a reconfigure does not
    # rebuild every bundle's Info.plist.
    configure_file("${_jusprin_plist}.edit" "${_jusprin_plist}" COPYONLY)

    # A target that names its own template keeps it.
    function(_jusprin_use_bundle_plist dir)
        get_property(_targets DIRECTORY "${dir}" PROPERTY BUILDSYSTEM_TARGETS)
        foreach (_target IN LISTS _targets)
            get_target_property(_type ${_target} TYPE)
            get_target_property(_bundle ${_target} MACOSX_BUNDLE)
            get_target_property(_own ${_target} MACOSX_BUNDLE_INFO_PLIST)
            if (_type STREQUAL "EXECUTABLE" AND _bundle AND NOT _own)
                set_target_properties(${_target} PROPERTIES MACOSX_BUNDLE_INFO_PLIST "${_jusprin_plist}")
            endif ()
        endforeach ()
        get_property(_subdirs DIRECTORY "${dir}" PROPERTY SUBDIRECTORIES)
        foreach (_subdir IN LISTS _subdirs)
            _jusprin_use_bundle_plist("${_subdir}")
        endforeach ()
    endfunction ()
    _jusprin_use_bundle_plist("${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}")
endif ()

content.content:
name: JusPrin release

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
#   users see nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
#   1.x used. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so in its
#   title.
#
# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
# jusprin-release/<anything>.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches:
      - 'jusprin-release/**'

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Check the version
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
    steps:
      - name: Only the release publisher
        env:
          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Test the release checks
        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs

      - name: Check the version against the releases
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json"
          gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/tags/" --jq '.[].ref' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt"
          node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs check src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Require the release notes
        run: |
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}.md"
          if [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
            echo "::error::Write $notes first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new."
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -q '^PLACEHOLDER' "$notes"; then
            echo "::warning::$notes is still the placeholder. Replace it before publishing the draft."
          fi

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.name }}
    needs: prepare
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Windows x64
            os: windows-latest
            arch: x64
          - name: macOS arm64
            os: macos-14
            arch: arm64
          - name: macOS x86_64
            os: macos-14
            arch: x86_64
          - name: Linux x64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            arch: ''
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
    secrets: inherit

  macos:
    name: macOS universal
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: macos-14
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      SIGN: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: Get both architectures
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-macOS-*
          path: mac_bundles
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Join them into the universal app
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/arm64 build/x86_64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_arm64.tar.gz -C build/arm64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_x86_64.tar.gz -C build/x86_64
          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x -1 -a universal -t 10.15

      # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml loads the certificate, with the secret
      # names JusPrin 1.x used.
      - name: Load the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          certificate="$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$certificate"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security default-keychain -s "$keychain"
          security import "$certificate" -P "$P12_PASSWORD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$keychain"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$keychain"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$P12_PASSWORD" "$keychain"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-macOS-universal
          path: dist/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  draft:
    name: Upload to the draft release
    needs: [prepare, build, macos]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Optional approval gate: give the "release" environment a required
    # reviewer in the repo settings.
    environment: release
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
      DRAFT_ID: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.draft_id }}
      PRERELEASE: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.prerelease }}
      SIGNED_MACOS: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging

      - name: Collect the files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-*
          path: collected
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Checksums
        run: |
          mkdir dist
          # The per-architecture Mac bundles only feed the universal app.
          find collected -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name 'JusPrin_Mac_bundle_*' -exec cp {} dist/ \;
          (cd dist && sha256sum -- * > SHA256SUMS.txt)
          cat dist/SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Create or update the draft
        run: |
          title="JusPrin $VERSION"
          if [ "$SIGNED_MACOS" != "true" ]; then
            title="$title (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)"
          else
            title="$title (Windows unsigned)"
          fi
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/$VERSION.md"
          prerelease=$([ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ] && echo --prerelease || echo --prerelease=false)
          if [ -z "$DRAFT_ID" ]; then
            gh release create "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft $prerelease \
              --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "$title" --notes-file "$notes"
          else
            # Never touch a published release: release.mjs only reports drafts.
            is_draft=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" --jq .draft)
            if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
              echo "::error::Release $DRAFT_ID is no longer a draft."
              exit 1
            fi
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" \
              -f target_commitish="$GITHUB_SHA" -f name="$title" -F prerelease="$PRERELEASE" \
              -f body="$(cat "$notes")" > /dev/null
            gh release upload "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          fi
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=20" \
            --jq ".[] | select(.tag_name == \"$TAG\") | {name, draft, prerelease, target_commitish, html_url, assets: [.assets[].name]}"
#############
name: JusPrin release build

# One platform of a JusPrin release, called by jusprin_release.yml.
#
# The build is OrcaSlicer's: its dependency workflow (build_deps.yml), cached
# under the key OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml uses, and its build
# scripts. Only the packaging is JusPrin's (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging).
# OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml can't be reused as it is: its Linux step looks
# for OrcaSlicer_Linux_V<version>.AppImage, which a JusPrin build never
# writes, and its packaging steps name everything OrcaSlicer.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      os:
        required: true
        type: string
      # x64 (Windows), arm64 or x86_64 (macOS); empty for Linux amd64, as in
      # OrcaSlicer's build_all.yml.

        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  cache:
    name: Find the deps cache
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    outputs:
      key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
      path: ${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
      hit: ${{ steps.lookup.outputs.cache-hit }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'
      - name: Compute the key
        id: key
        shell: bash
        env:
          # As in OrcaSlicer's build_check_cache.yml. The macOS and Linux trees are
          # OrcaSlicer's and share its cache; OrcaSlicer builds Windows with clang-cl,
          # so JusPrin's cl tree is cached on its own.

          echo "key=${cache_os}-cache-orcaslicer_deps-build-${{ hashFiles('deps/**') }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

          echo "path=deps/build${dep_folder}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

        id: lookup
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ steps.key.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ steps.key.outputs.key }}
          lookup-only: true

  deps:
    name: Build deps
    needs: cache
    if: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.hit != 'true' }}
    uses: ./.github/workflows/build_deps.yml
    with:
      cache-key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
      cache-path: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
      valid-cache: false
      os: ${{ inputs.os }}
      arch: ${{ inputs.arch }}
      # cl under the Visual Studio generator, which JusPrin's Windows build uses.
      compiler: msvc
      # Stops build_deps.yml before it calls OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      build-deps-only: true
    secrets: inherit

  build:
    name: Build JusPrin
    needs: [cache, deps]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.cache.result == 'success' && (needs.deps.result == 'success' || needs.deps.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.os }}
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - name: Load the deps
        uses: actions/cache@v5
        with:
          path: ${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}
          key: ${{ needs.cache.outputs.key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true

      # The same CMake as OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml.
      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      # The Agent and Home pages are built with npm (JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt).
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      # Windows
      - name: Set up MSVC
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        uses: microsoft/setup-msbuild@v3

      - name: Install NSIS
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: choco install nsis

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml calls build_win.bat, but with cl rather than
        # clang-cl. -i installs into build\OrcaSlicer, which the packaging reads.
        run: |
          $deps = (Split-Path "${{ github.workspace }}/${{ needs.cache.outputs.path }}").Replace('\', '/')
          .\build_win.bat -s -i --arch ${{ inputs.arch }} --build-dir build --deps-dir $deps --msvc --msbuild

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/windows_package.ps1 -BuildDir build -Version $env:VERSION `
            -Arch "${{ inputs.arch }}" -OutDir dist

      # macOS: each architecture is built here; jusprin_release.yml joins them
      # into the universal app and the disk image.
      - name: Prepare the Mac
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          brew install libtool
          mkdir -p "${{ github.workspace }}/deps/build/${{ inputs.arch }}"
          # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml does, for disk space.
          sudo find /Applications -maxdepth 1 -type d -name "Xcode_*.app" ! -name "Xcode_15.4.app" -exec rm -rf {} +
          sudo rm -rf ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Caches/*

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: ./build_release_macos.sh -s -n -x -j 3 -a ${{ inputs.arch }} -t 10.15

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          mkdir -p dist
          tar -czf "dist/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_${{ inputs.arch }}.tar.gz" -C "build/${{ inputs.arch }}" OrcaSlicer

      # Linux
      - name: Install the build packages
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        uses: ./.github/actions/apt-install-deps

      - name: Build
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          # -s builds the slicer and lays out build/package; JusPrin's AppImage
          # replaces OrcaSlicer's (-i).
          ./build_linux.sh -srlL
          ./scripts/check_appimage_libs.sh ./build/package ./build/package/bin/orca-slicer

      - name: Package
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/appimage.sh build/package "$VERSION" \
            "dist/JusPrin_Linux_AppImage_Ubuntu2404_V${VERSION}${{ inputs.arch && format('_{0}', inputs.arch) || '' }}.AppImage"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-${{ runner.os }}-${{ inputs.arch || 'x64' }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          # The release keeps the files; these only carry them to it.
          retention-days: 7

name: JusPrin release

# Builds JusPrin from one commit and uploads the files to a DRAFT GitHub
# release. It never publishes anything.
#
# - The version is the one in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp, and
#   the draft is tagged jusprin/v<version>, as JusPrin 1.4.0 was (the repo
#   still holds OrcaSlicer's own v2.x tags). GitHub creates that tag only when
#   the draft is published, by hand, on the Releases page. JusPrin's update
#   check reads the public release list, which never includes drafts, so
#   users see nothing until then.
# - It stops if that version is already released, is not above every
#   released JusPrin version, or its tag already exists
#   (Packaging/release.mjs), and if
#   Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md, the notes the draft starts with and
#   that the app shows under "What's new", is missing.
# - Running it again for the same version replaces the draft's files.
# - Files: Windows x64 installer and portable zip, macOS universal disk image,
#   Linux x64 AppImage, and SHA256SUMS.txt.
# - Only the release publisher can run it: the repo variable
#   JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER, or kennethjiang when it is unset.
# - Signing: macOS when "sign_macos" is ticked, with the Apple secrets JusPrin
#   1.x used. Windows builds are unsigned. An unsigned draft says so in its
#   title.
#
# Start it from Actions > JusPrin release > Run workflow (the file must also
# be on the default branch for that button), or by pushing a branch named
# jusprin-release/<anything>.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sign_macos:
        description: 'Sign and notarise the macOS app with the Apple secrets'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push:
    branches:
      - 'jusprin-release/**'

permissions:
  contents: write   # create the draft and upload its files
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: jusprin-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    name: Check the version
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.check.outputs.tag }}
      prerelease: ${{ steps.check.outputs.prerelease }}
      draft_id: ${{ steps.check.outputs.draft_id }}
    steps:
      - name: Only the release publisher
        env:
          PUBLISHER: ${{ vars.JUSPRIN_RELEASE_PUBLISHER || 'kennethjiang' }}
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_ACTOR" != "$PUBLISHER" ]; then
            echo "::error::Only @$PUBLISHER may make a JusPrin release (this run is @$GITHUB_ACTOR's)."
            exit 1
          fi

      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Test the release checks
        run: node --test src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.test.mjs

      - name: Check the version against the releases
        id: check
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=100" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json"
          gh api --paginate "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/tags/" --jq '.[].ref' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt"
          node src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release.mjs check src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/releases.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/tags.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Require the release notes
        run: |
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}.md"
          if [ ! -s "$notes" ]; then
            echo "::error::Write $notes first. The draft starts with it and the app shows it under What's new."
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -q '^PLACEHOLDER' "$notes"; then
            echo "::warning::$notes is still the placeholder. Replace it before publishing the draft."
          fi

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.name }}
    needs: prepare
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Windows x64
            os: windows-latest
            arch: x64
          - name: macOS arm64
            os: macos-14
            arch: arm64
          - name: macOS x86_64
            os: macos-14
            arch: x86_64
          - name: Linux x64
            os: ubuntu-24.04
            arch: ''
    uses: ./.github/workflows/jusprin_release_build.yml
    with:
      os: ${{ matrix.os }}
      arch: ${{ matrix.arch }}
      version: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
    secrets: inherit

  macos:
    name: macOS universal
    needs: [prepare, build]
    runs-on: macos-14
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      SIGN: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          lfs: 'false'

      - uses: lukka/get-cmake@latest
        with:
          cmakeVersion: "~4.3.0"
          useLocalCache: true
          useCloudCache: true

      - name: Get both architectures
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-macOS-*
          path: mac_bundles
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Join them into the universal app
        run: |
          mkdir -p build/arm64 build/x86_64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_arm64.tar.gz -C build/arm64
          tar -xzf mac_bundles/JusPrin_Mac_bundle_x86_64.tar.gz -C build/x86_64
          ./build_release_macos.sh -u -x -1 -a universal -t 10.15

      # As OrcaSlicer's build_orca.yml loads the certificate, with the secret
      # names JusPrin 1.x used.
      - name: Load the signing certificate
        if: env.SIGN == '1'
        env:
          BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64 }}
          P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.P12_PASSWORD }}
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          certificate="$RUNNER_TEMP/build_certificate.p12"
          keychain="$RUNNER_TEMP/app-signing.keychain-db"
          echo -n "$BUILD_CERTIFICATE_BASE64" | base64 --decode --output "$certificate"
          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$keychain"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$keychain"
          security default-keychain -s "$keychain"
          security import "$certificate" -P "$P12_PASSWORD" -A -t cert -f pkcs12 -k "$keychain"
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$keychain"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple:,codesign: -s -k "$P12_PASSWORD" "$keychain"

      - name: Make the disk image
        env:
          JUSPRIN_SIGN: ${{ env.SIGN }}
          MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERTIFICATE_ID }}
          APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.APPLE_DEV_ACCOUNT }}
          TEAM_ID: ${{ secrets.TEAM_ID }}
          APP_PWD: ${{ secrets.APP_PWD }}
        run: |
          ./src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/macos_package.sh \
            build/universal/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer.app "$VERSION" dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: jusprin-macOS-universal
          path: dist/*.dmg
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  draft:
    name: Upload to the draft release
    needs: [prepare, build, macos]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Optional approval gate: give the "release" environment a required
    # reviewer in the repo settings.
    environment: release
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      VERSION: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.version }}
      TAG: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.tag }}
      DRAFT_ID: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.draft_id }}
      PRERELEASE: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.prerelease }}
      SIGNED_MACOS: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.sign_macos || false }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          sparse-checkout: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging

      - name: Collect the files
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: jusprin-*
          path: collected
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Checksums
        run: |
          mkdir dist
          # The per-architecture Mac bundles only feed the universal app.
          find collected -maxdepth 1 -type f ! -name 'JusPrin_Mac_bundle_*' -exec cp {} dist/ \;
          (cd dist && sha256sum -- * > SHA256SUMS.txt)
          cat dist/SHA256SUMS.txt

      - name: Create or update the draft
        run: |
          title="JusPrin $VERSION"
          if [ "$SIGNED_MACOS" != "true" ]; then
            title="$title (UNSIGNED TEST BUILD: do not publish)"
          else
            title="$title (Windows unsigned)"
          fi
          notes="src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/$VERSION.md"
          prerelease=$([ "$PRERELEASE" = "true" ] && echo --prerelease || echo --prerelease=false)
          if [ -z "$DRAFT_ID" ]; then
            gh release create "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --draft $prerelease \
              --target "$GITHUB_SHA" --title "$title" --notes-file "$notes"
          else
            # Never touch a published release: release.mjs only reports drafts.
            is_draft=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" --jq .draft)
            if [ "$is_draft" != "true" ]; then
              echo "::error::Release $DRAFT_ID is no longer a draft."
              exit 1
            fi
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases/$DRAFT_ID" \
              -f target_commitish="$GITHUB_SHA" -f name="$title" -F prerelease="$PRERELEASE" \
              -f body="$(cat "$notes")" > /dev/null
            gh release upload "$TAG" dist/* --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          fi
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/releases?per_page=20" \
            --jq ".[] | select(.tag_name == \"$TAG\") | {name, draft, prerelease, target_commitish, html_url, assets: [.assets[].name]}"

name: Build all

on:
  push:
    branches:
     - main
     - release/*
    paths:
     - 'deps/**'
     - 'src/**'
     - '**/CMakeLists.txt'
     - 'version.inc'
     - 'localization/**'
     - 'resources/**'
     - ".github/workflows/build_*.yml"
     - 'scripts/flatpak/**'

  pull_request:
    branches:
     - main
     - release/*
    paths:
     - 'deps/**'
     - 'src/**'
     - '**/CMakeLists.txt'
     - 'version.inc'
     - ".github/workflows/build_*.yml"
     - 'build_linux.sh'
     - 'build_release_vs2022.bat'
     - 'build_release_macos.sh'
     - 'scripts/flatpak/**'

  schedule:
      - cron: '35 7 * * *' # run once a day near midnight US Pacific time

  workflow_dispatch: # allows for manual dispatch
    inputs:
      build-deps-only:
        description: 'Only build dependencies (bypasses caching)'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

JusPrin

**Welcome to JusPrin, the first GenAI app for 3D printing!** Brought to you by the creator of [The Spaghetti Detective](https://www.thespaghettidetective.com/), JusPrin aims to revolutionize the 3D printing experience by eliminating the need for manual slicing. Imagine: **no confusing slicing parameters, no headaches over printing issues caused by incorrect settings. Just print.** That's the promise of JusPrin. ## Table of Contents - [Why JusPrin?](#why-jusprin) - [Download](#download) - [Getting Started](#getting-started) - [Feedback](#feedback) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) ## Why JusPrin? 3D printing enthusiasts have relied on slicing tools to prepare models, often struggling with complex parameters and trial-and-error setups. JusPrin changes that by putting AI in charge of the slicing settings. You say what you want the print to do, and AI picks and tunes the settings for your printer and filament. - **Eliminate Complexity**: No need to tweak dozens of parameters. AI takes care of it. - **Fix Failed Prints**: Show AI a photo of what went wrong. It reads your file, your settings and your slice, changes the settings and slices again. - **Stay in Control**: You choose the printer, the filament and what the print is for, and you decide when to print. Every setting is still there when you want it. JusPrin is available for **Windows**, **macOS** and **Linux**. ## Download 📥 **[Download the Latest Release](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest)** ## Getting Started 1. **Download and open JusPrin.** 2. **Choose how AI runs**: sign in to a JusPrin account, use your own API key, or connect Claude Code or Claude Desktop. You can also just slice for now and set up AI later in Preferences. 3. **Add your printer**: JusPrin can bring in the printers you set up in JusPrin 1 or OrcaSlicer. 4. **Open a model**: STL, OBJ, STEP or 3MF. 5. **Ask AI**: tell it what the print is for, even if you're not sure which settings that needs. It suggests settings from your model and slices. 6. **Print**: send the print to your printer, or export the sliced file. ## Feedback Your feedback is invaluable! If something goes wrong or a setting doesn't look right, use **Help › Report a problem…** in the app, which opens a GitHub issue with your app version filled in. You can also write to [jusprin-support@obico.io](mailto:jusprin-support@obico.io). Every bit of feedback helps JusPrin become a better, smarter tool for everyone. ## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). To report a security problem, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). JusPrin 1 lives on the [`jusprin-v1`](https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/tree/jusprin-v1) branch. ## License JusPrin is open-source software licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, based on Orca Slicer. Orca Slicer is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3. Orca Slicer is based on Bambu Studio by BambuLab. Bambu Studio is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3. Bambu Studio is based on PrusaSlicer by PrusaResearch. PrusaSlicer is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3. PrusaSlicer is owned by Prusa Research. PrusaSlicer is originally based on Slic3r by Alessandro Ranellucci. Slic3r is licensed under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3. Slic3r was created by Alessandro Ranellucci with the help of many other contributors. The GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 ensures that if you use any part of this software in any way (even behind a web server), your software must be released under the same license. Orca Slicer includes a pressure advance calibration pattern test adapted from Andrew Ellis' generator, which is licensed under GNU General Public License, version 3. Ellis' generator is itself adapted from a generator developed by Sineos for Marlin, which is licensed under GNU General Public License, version 3. The Bambu networking plugin is based on non-free libraries from BambuLab. It is optional to the Orca Slicer and provides extended functionalities for Bambulab printer users. **A heartfelt thank you to [OrcaSlicer](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer) for providing the foundation on which JusPrin is built!**
